sophie: quick check — after int8 quant on new-vec-1 I see recall@10 drop on prod-sampled from ~0.82 -> 0.75 :thinking_face: anyone else seeing this?
liam: which eval dataset and seed? full production sample or tiny test?
sophie: prod-1m-sampled (stratified by cohort), seed=42. pipeline: faiss-hnsw, cosine, k=10. ran the usual eval harness.
liam: can you paste the command you ran?
sophie: sure
sophie: ```
python eval_embeddings.py \
  --model new-vec-1-int8 \
  --data prod-1m-sampled \
  --index faiss_hnsw \
  --metric cosine \
  --k 10 \
  --seed 42
```
sophie: full log: eva-bot job attached (id 1780000010)
eva-bot: evaluation job 1780000010 queued
ana: quick question — is this quantization-only (weights) or activation quant too?
sophie: weights-only int8 via our quant tool; no activation quant. I also tried the fp16 baseline for comparison.
jon: odds are it's cohort-specific. Did you split recall by cohort? billing/faq/enterprise?
sophie: good call — per-cohort recall below:
- faq: 0.86 -> 0.85
- billing: 0.81 -> 0.69  <-- big drop
- product-titles: 0.78 -> 0.74
sophie: so billing cohort seems hammered.
ana: can you paste a couple of top failing queries from billing?
sophie: here are three queries where top-1 changed from correct -> wrong after quant:
1) "how do i update billing address"  => expected: doc_452, quant top1: doc_87
2) "refund processing time" => expected: doc_91, quant top1: doc_11
3) "add payment method v2" => expected: doc_374, quant top1: doc_374 (ok for this one)
liam: this smells like directional changes in embeddings for billing tokens (maybe rare tokens or tokenization edge case). did you compare cosine similarity deltas for positives vs negatives?
sophie: yes, avg pos cos dropped from 0.72 -> 0.65 for billing, negatives unchanged ~0.12.
jon: two quick experiments: 1) normalize before indexing (cosine expects normalized vectors), 2) check faiss index params (efsearch). sometimes small quant noise matters more with low ef.
liam: also try re-indexing with longer pq/ivf training or increase efConstruction/efSearch. what efSearch did you have?
sophie: efSearch=64 (default). will try efSearch=256.
ana: another angle: run L2 vs cosine. If you didn't normalize after quant, cosine will break. snippet to normalize:
ana: ```python
emb = emb / np.linalg.norm(emb, axis=1, keepdims=True)
```
sophie: good point — we normalized for fp16 baseline but I realize normalization step was accidentally skipped in quant pipeline. oof.
liam: that could explain a lot. try re-running with normalization + efSearch=256 and post results.
sophie: will run now. kicking off job.
eva-bot: evaluation job 1780000247 queued
sophie: while that's running — jon any thoughts on quant recipe? we used symmetric per-channel. maybe asymmetric per-tensor for this model?
jon: try per-channel weight quant + fp16 activations. also we have a 4-bit smooth quant prototype that sometimes preserves inter-vector angles better. tradeoff: throughput.
sophie: ok will test 4-bit smooth later if normalization fix doesn't close gap.
liam: also create a small viz — UMAP of billing cohort pre/post quant to see cluster drift. often it's a rotation/flip causing nearest neighbors to jump.
sophie: plotting now, sending screenshot in thread (not included here) — looks like a small split in the billing cluster post-quant.
ana: if cluster purity drops, compute cluster purity metric: for each cluster, fraction of points with same label, then mean. can you run cluster_analysis?
sophie: running: `python cluster_analysis.py --emb new-vec-1-int8 --cohort billing --n_clusters 50` (job id 1780000301)
eva-bot: job 1780000301 finished: mean_cluster_purity down 0.03 vs baseline
sophie: ok that's consistent. plan: 1) re-run quant pipeline with explicit normalization + efSearch=256, 2) test per-channel asymmetric weights, 3) if still bad, try 4-bit smooth. also add cohort-level monitors to onboarding dashboard.
liam: +1. also add a small regression check that fails onboarding if any cohort recall@10 drops > 0.04.
ana: I'll open a quick PR to add cohort checks to eval harness.
sophie: scheduling 30m sync tomorrow to triage if fixes don't close gap. volunteers?
liam: I can join.
jon: me too.
ana: me as well.
sophie: thanks all :thumbsup: will post updated numbers when jobs finish :eyes:
